neet_phy_u07_t01_1.working: Fluids cannot sustain shear stress or a definite length, so they have no rigidity or Young's modulus. They resist volume change, so they have bulk modulus only.

neet_phy_u07_t01_3.working: Extension under own weight is ΔL = ρgL²/(2Y), which does not depend on radius. Y has length 2L, so ΔL_Y/ΔL_X = (2L)²/L² = 4.

neet_phy_u07_t01_4.working: Young's modulus relates to change in length (IV). Bulk modulus relates to change in volume (III). Modulus of rigidity relates to change in shape (I). Compressibility is the reciprocal of bulk modulus (II).

neet_phy_u07_t01_5.working: A is true in the standard textbook sense: G = Y/(2(1+σ)), giving G ≈ Y/3 for typical σ. B is true: Poisson's ratio is dimensionless with theoretical range -1 to 0.5. C is false: Y is a material property, independent of length. D is true: energy density = stress²/(2Y). E is false: a thicker wire has larger area, so it extends less. Correct set is A, B and D.
